notes: Reconstructed by tools/tubuild.py create and then reconciled by hand. The file's own header comment records the two decisions that are load-bearing: `#pragma defer_codegen off` over ordinals 0 and 1 so the `opt_common_subs off` bracket binds to ordinal 1 alone, and the resulting split emission order (parse-time half ascending, deferred half descending).

tubuild create reported one declaration CONFLICT, `func_ov001_020aa6cc`, declared `void func_ov001_020aa6cc(int r0)` by the legacy source for ordinal 1 and `void func_ov001_020aa6cc(int character)` by the one for ordinal 0. The two spellings differ only in the parameter name, so the merged TU keeps one declaration; nothing was left commented out.

The head array data_ov001_020ad634 was declared three ways across the legacy shards (`dCapIcon_c *[]`, `void *[]`, `int[]`). The node-pointer view is the complete one -- ordinal 0 walks the nodes -- and is the one the TU keeps; ordinal 1 takes one added cast at its store and is byte-identical with it.

Five extern declarations were reconciled against the rest of the tree after tools/check_decl_agreement.py flagged them: data_0209f3e8 is spelt `int[]` (the plurality) with the dActor_c* view moved to a cast at the use site, data_ov001_020ad620 and data_ov001_020ad624 are scalars rather than arrays, func_ov001_020aa6b0 takes `int *` as its definition does, and SaveData::IsCharacterUnlocked is called through include/SaveData.h instead of a flat mangled extern. The cast on the slot-table compare has to be on the LEFT operand: `data_0209f3e8[mSlot] == (int)mOwner` swaps two register assignments in ordinal 0 and costs three words. All six functions were re-verified byte-exact afterwards, and tools/rombuild.py rebuilt the full ROM to the same sha256 d1506e90efae5e2d2cf119926a4ac2a291bd5ca78349d09d5024e1a918c478e8 as the source-independent control. The verification.linkcheck record below predates that reconciliation; the full-ROM rombuild run is what proves the final source.
